headword: {豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし}
gloss: Toyotomi Hideyoshi (1537-1598), warlord who completed the unification of Japan

definitions.gloss: Toyotomi Hideyoshi, warlord who unified Japan
definitions.explanation: A general who rose from peasant origins to become {織田信長|おだのぶなが}'s most trusted commander, and after Nobunaga's death completed the unification of Japan. His rise from a common foot soldier to the country's supreme ruler makes him the archetype of the self-made man in Japanese history.

examples.japanese: {豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{農民|のうみん}→農民：03759_noumin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出身|しゅっしん}→出身：03221_shusshin⟧だった。
examples.english: Toyotomi Hideyoshi came from a peasant background.

examples.japanese: {秀吉|ひでよし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{信長|のぶなが}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{死後|しご}→死後：21150_shigo⟧、⟦{天下|てんか}→天下：12188_tenka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{統一|とういつ}→統一：04551_touitsu⟧した。
examples.english: After Nobunaga's death, Hideyoshi unified the country.

examples.japanese: {秀吉|ひでよし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{百姓|ひゃくしょう}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{天下人|てんかびと}にまで⟦{上|のぼ}り→上り：03943_nobori⟧⟦{詰|つ}めた→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧{立志伝中|りっしでんちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Hideyoshi is a rags-to-riches figure who rose from a peasant to the ruler of all Japan.

notes:
{豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし} is the second of the three great unifiers of Japan, following ⟦{織田信長|おだのぶなが}→織田信長：30992_odanobunaga⟧ and preceding {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}. He began as a low-ranking foot soldier and rose through talent and political skill to become supreme ruler, making him the classic Japanese rags-to-riches figure.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Nicknamed ⟦{猿|さる}→猿：02213_saru⟧ ("monkey") by Nobunaga for his appearance, a detail widely known from period dramas and fiction.
- Famous for grand displays of power such as the {醍醐|だいご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧ (a lavish cherry-blossom viewing party) and for building {大坂城|おおさかじょう} (Osaka Castle).
- A well-known saying, "if the cuckoo won't sing, make it want to sing," is attributed to him and used to contrast his persuasive style with {信長|のぶなが}'s ruthlessness and {家康|いえやす}'s patience.
- His attempted invasions of Korea in the 1590s are also a standard reference point in discussions of the period.
